Method of Attack: Handling mixed-format IP addresses improperly, leading to anti-Server-Side Request Forgery (SSRF) bypasses to Remote File Inclusion (RFI).
Discoverer: Victor Viale, Sick Codes, Nick Sahler, Kelly Kaoudis, John Jackson
Impacted Systems: Applications using the netmask library for IP parsing, such as hundreds of thousands of applications that parse IPv4 addresses and CIDR blocks or compare them, and around 278,000 GitHub repositories.
Attack Vector: Exploits the way netmask handles mixed-format IP addresses, more specifically when a decimal IPv4 address contains a leading zero.
Indicators of Compromise: Misinterpretation of IP addresses due to the presence of leading zeros, leading to a different IP address being seen by netmask due to improper validations.

Method of Attack: Similar to netmask, handles mixed-format IP addresses improperly, leading to security flaws.
Impacted Systems: Applications using the Perl components Netmask and some others (e.g. Net-IPAddress-Util, Net-CIDR-Lite, Net-CIDR, etc.)
Attack Vector: Exploits the way Net::Netmask handles mixed-format IP addresses, more specifically when a decimal IPv4 address contains a leading zero.
Indicators of Compromise: Misinterpretation of IP addresses due to the presence of leading zeros, leading to a different IP address being seen by Net::Netmask due to improper validations.
